Source contracts: src/agent_runtime/permission_scopes.py

src/agent_runtime/permission_scopes.py

Python · Tier A

Resolve user permission hierarchy and apply revision-checked grants across settings, chats and native runs. PermissionAuthority dispatches to MemoryPermissionAuthority for the live Controller RAM hub; this file also implements standalone attached-SQL transactions and shared precedence/grant logic. Audit records retain modes and revisions without prompts or rule bodies; policy evaluation and exact execution consent have separate collaborators.

Significant symbols

Symbol Line Documentation
PermissionConflict 29 Report a stale policy edit or an approval that no longer matches the waiting run, so callers cannot silently overwrite newer user authority.
audit_schema 35 Create the standalone permission-change audit table if absent. Its monotonically increasing sequence supports bounded retention; callers own transaction completion.
audit 45 Append scope, revision and previous/current modes in the same SQL transaction as a policy edit, then retain at most the latest thousand sequence positions. Rules and prompt contents are deliberately absent; the schema name is an internal constant.
PermissionAuthority 65 One installation/profile's authority, with atomic revision-checked writes.
PermissionAuthority.connect 87 Open a managed native-run SQLite connection and attach chat/settings databases so a permission grant and pending-run update can commit together. This path is for standalone stores; the RAM subclass forbids SQL access.
PermissionAuthority.initialize_global 96 Create an inherited global permission record at revision zero only when none exists, using an immediate transaction. Existing saved policy and revision remain untouched.
PermissionAuthority.read_in 118 Read a scope's nullable policy and revision from the caller's attached databases. Global or prompt absence means inherited revision zero; a nonexistent conversation raises. Internal callers must supply a supported scope because the final branch addresses prompt records.
PermissionAuthority.write_in 150 Normalize the complete policy, check the optional expected revision, replace the selected scope and append its bounded audit record inside the caller's transaction. Increment revision even for a reset to inheritance; return the stored canonical policy and new revision.
PermissionAuthority.set 193 Begin an immediate policy-edit transaction and reject prompt edits for a missing or ended native run before delegating revision checking and persistence. Conversation/global edits affect live resolution without rewriting every run.
PermissionAuthority.resolve_in 246 Resolve Prompt, Conversation, Global then Manual default within the caller's view. Prefer persisted prompt overrides and preserve explicit legacy run snapshots; tolerate a missing historical conversation reference for scheduled work. Return the chosen policy/source/revision plus all scope records without network or model calls.
PermissionAuthority.resolve 293 Open a read transaction and return one effective permission view for the supplied context and explicit scope identities. The RAM subclass uses an immutable hub view instead.
PermissionAuthority.apply 300 Resolve current authority, apply its canonical policy/approval mode to the mutable execution context, and attach the chosen source and revision for downstream authorization and display.
PermissionAuthority.grant 311 Apply a pending grant under an immediate standalone SQL transaction so scope edits, audit and resumed run state succeed or roll back together.
PermissionAuthority.grant_in 321 Validate the grant against an unowned run still awaiting the exact pending confirmation. Match rule scope to that operation, compare the requested revision, preserve narrower overrides and update policy, resume context and run authority within the caller's transaction. This grants reusable user permission; capability, credential and hard-safety checks remain separate.
